title: [finding] the sdui-parser lockstep has drifted again since the record was taken: objectui carries 26 diagnostic codes, this copy 24 — `inert-quick-add` and `member-type-mismatch` exist only on the renderer side
body:
Surfaced while porting objectstack#13957 into objectui (objectui#7235, objectui PR for branch `claude/issue-7235-html-tier-discriminator-attr`). Filed rather than folded in: that port is objectui-only and adds **zero** diagnostic codes; this is a pre-existing divergence it merely made visible.

## The contract

objectstack#12719 states the invariant `scripts/check-sdui-lockstep.mjs` mechanises, quoted from the checker's own header:

> both copies byte-agree on the accepted grammar and on diagnostic codes.

## The measurement

Taken with **this repo's own extractor** (`fingerprintOf` from `scripts/check-sdui-lockstep.mjs`), run against three trees — no hand-rolled parallel implementation:

| tree | source files | diagnostic codes |
|---|---|---|
| objectstack (this copy, today) | 7 | **24** |
| objectui at the pinned rev `53ded82bf7a4` | 7 | 24 |
| objectui `origin/main` `567f3701` (today) | 8 | **26** |

- present in objectui, absent here: `inert-quick-add`, `member-type-mismatch`
- present here, absent in objectui: none — the drift is one-directional
- the extra objectui source file is `packages/sdui-parser/src/kanban-quick-add.ts`

The two codes trace to objectui#8285 (kanban Quick Add reported rather than dropped) and objectui#8067 (member-kind unions). Both landed in objectui **after** 2026-09-05, which is the date the vendored record was taken — so both are inside the blind spot the checker's own header names:

> CANNOT see objectui moving AFTER the record was taken. That direction needs objectui at check time, which is the shape this repo declined.

## Why this is a finding and not noise

1. **The gate is green today and will red at the next pin bump.** `pnpm check:sdui-lockstep` passes right now (measured: self-test exit 0, gate exit 0, "agrees on all 24 diagnostic code(s)"). It compares THIS tree against the record, and the record still describes the 24-code objectui of 2026-09-05. The moment `.objectui-sha` moves and `pnpm gen:sdui-lockstep` re-records, the record gains two codes this copy does not have, and the gate reds — naming a divergence whose cause is six days old and nothing to do with whichever PR happens to be bumping the pin.
2. **The harm the invariant exists to stop is live in the meantime.** A renderer that can emit a diagnostic the save gate never emits is the dialect split objectstack#12719 describes, in the direction where the save gate is the more permissive of the two.
3. **The pattern already has two closed precedents** — objectstack#12719 (`inert-expression`) and objectstack#12814 (union-arm `type-mismatch`) — each a code that landed in objectui first and was ported here afterwards. This is the third instance, so it is a recurrence of a known class rather than a novel one.

## What is NOT claimed here

- ⛔ This is not a claim that the two codes should be ported as-is. `inert-quick-add` concerns a control gated on a runtime slot no parsed page can write, which may be a genuinely renderer-only concern; that judgement is the porting decision, not this card's.
- ⛔ It is not a claim that the pinned record is wrong. The record correctly describes objectui at `53ded82bf7a4`.
- The two-code gap and the one-file gap are measured; whether either is deliberate is not.

## Reproduction (zero network, zero build beyond an install)

```
node -e "import('./scripts/check-sdui-lockstep.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.fingerprintOf('.').codes.length))"
```

…then the same `fingerprintOf` against a materialised objectui `origin/main` `packages/sdui-parser/src` tree. Both numbers above came out of exactly that, in one container, minutes apart. The control that keeps the difference from being an artefact of the extractor pre-exists the reading: the SAME extractor, on the SAME objectui repo, at the PINNED revision, returns 24 and the matching file list — so it is demonstrably sensitive to the class of drift being reported, and the 26 is not a quirk of how it was invoked.

Raised by an ObjectStack development agent working objectui#7235; the objectui-side port itself is unaffected and adds no code to either set (its before/after fingerprints are byte-identical).
